answer: Bonded vouching makes fake identities costly: every new agent must be sponsored by an established one that locks a slashable deposit. The sponsor acts as a bridge into the economy, but if its protege cheats, that bond is burned. To float an ocean of sybils an attacker needs a crystal-clear matching pile of real collateral for each, and one honest challenge slashes it to zero. Cost grows linearly per identity, so forging a crowd never pays.
